notes: Context: Mid-market SaaS (analytics), product-led growth. Evaluating Hosted API for dev ramp, moving toward Dedicated for predictable latency and data isolation.

POC summary: Hosted API used to validate integration and prompt templates. Metrics: embeddings quality OK (cosine mean 0.78 on eval set), doc-search relevance edges acceptable. Pain: token spend variability during overnight batch jobs.

Tech targets: p95 generation latency < 250ms for short prompts (chat/FAQ), sustained throughput target ~150 QPS at 512-token average, occasional spikes to 400 QPS during release day. Embeddings latency target < 120ms per request for bulk indexing.

Model preference: prefer open model family (quantized Llama2-70B-ish equivalent) for most traffic; willing to use smaller distill/quant variants for burst to control cost. Want ability to pin model versions and automatic fallback when capacity constrained.
Security/Compliance: must have SOC2, SSO (SAML), audit logs to satisfy SOC/compliance team. Data residency preference: US only for PII-containing documents; full retention control required.

Commercial ask (Riverbend): seeking Dedicated commit that balances predictable unit costs with ability to absorb release-day spikes. Initial request: monthly commit equivalent to 4 reserved GPUs with guaranteed baseline throughput + 2x burst without pre-approval for up to 48 hours.

Redwood proposal (initial): three-tier commit schedule: 1) 4 GPU-equivalent baseline commit: $22k/mo, 2) 8 GPU-equivalent baseline: $40k/mo, 3) Enterprise 16 GPUs: custom. Burst policy: up to 1.5x baseline for up to 24 hours; overage billed at 1.8x unit rate. Ramp incentives: 3-month credit on first month for annual commit.

Riverbend counter: needs 2x burst for release windows (up to 48 hours), capped overage to protect burn (suggested cap $10k/mo), and an explicit ramp schedule (month1 40% commit, month2 70%, month3 100%) to avoid immediate long-term spend.

Negotiation notes: AE (Maya) and SE (Liam) proposed a compromise: 4-GPU baseline at $20k/mo with burst up to 2x for first 2 months (no overage charge for burst up to a cumulative 500k tokens), then standard overage at 1.6x. Redwood would include a one-time onboarding credit of $5k and 30 days extended observability retention for free.

Engineering concerns (Ben, CTO): need SLA for p95 < 300ms at baseline, fallback routing documented, KV cache warmup plan during scaled rollouts. Also need clear rollback/fallback behavior if Dedicated capacity is throttled.

Legal/Procurement: reviewing SOW language around data residency and indemnity. Procurement asked for a simple overage cap and an exit clause tied to 60-day notice after first year. Legal requested sample SOC2 report and KMS integration spec (Liam provided links).
POC artifacts: drive:/pocs/Riverbend/poctest-results-02-26.xlsx contains throughput/latency curves for 4 vs 8-node configs. SE notes attached in Drive (see linked docs).

Open technical blockers: 1) engineering wants 95th percentile cold-start times for KV cache on model variants, 2) confirmation that prefix caching will survive short bursts without rollback, 3) VPC peering checklist from infra (listed in drive doc).
Commercial blockers: final signoff from CFO on $20k+/mo baseline; Procurement wants overage cap and clearer ramp credits spelled out in SOW.

Next steps agreed: finalize committed level (likely 4 GPU baseline with ramp schedule), write SOW with burst terms and overage cap, legal to exchange paperwork next week (target SOW draft by 2026-03-17).
Quote from Ben (CTO): 'We need predictable tail-latency and a burst policy that doesn't require us to babysit runs — if Redwood can give us that, Dedicated makes sense.'
Chatter: engineering asked if Redwood Optimize recommendations (quantization + batching) can be included as part of onboarding. SE confirmed a workshop included in onboarding credits.
